exact_prompt: Create a single publication-quality landscape 3:2 narrative illustration for an adult illustrated English-reading booklet. Finished standalone artwork, not a book mockup, not a collage of multiple unrelated panels. Sophisticated contemporary editorial gouache and watercolor, carefully controlled colored-pencil accents, velvety matte paint, subtle warm paper texture, soft natural daylight. Warm ivory paper dominates; subdued eucalyptus and sage greens structure the composition; restrained buttery lemon-yellow and dusty terracotta accents. Calm, comfortable, refined, credible drawing and natural anatomy. An airy coherent composition with one clear story focal point and at most two supporting details, generous breathing room at all edges and softly feathered painted edges into ivory. Detailed but uncluttered. Historically and scientifically appropriate objects, clothing and setting. Show the particular article's pivotal event or mechanism rather than a generic portrait or generic textbook symbols. Human figures treated with dignity; no grotesque caricature, no sensational violence or visible injuries. Absolutely no typography, captions, letters, numbers, logos, watermarks, diagram labels, fake writing or invented charts anywhere. Avoid corporate vector icons, slick 3D rendering and childish cartoon style. High-quality, print-ready visual storytelling, matching a warm ivory-and-sage adult watercolor booklet. ARTICLE61 scene: a calm early-1960s working port, showing how a standardized freight container can move between ship and road without unloading its contents. One plain unmarked muted-sage steel container is the clear focal point, gently suspended level by a credible dock crane and corner lifting fittings just above an empty flatbed lorry. Supporting detail one is the flatbed lorry in accurate early-1960s shape. Supporting detail two is a modest low-deck cargo vessel at the quay behind, not a modern enormous container ship; it carries a few similar steel boxes. A soft quiet harbour and ivory sky surround the scene. Strong readable spatial relationships: the container is separate from the lorry chassis, there are no wheels attached to the suspended box, four-corner lifting is physically coherent, the quay is dry land next to the water. Paint the practical transport mechanism, not world maps, economics charts, flying containers, or any written markings. View in gentle three-quarter perspective with warm daylight, breathing space and no crowd.

notes: Early-1960s intermodal loading illustrated; not presented as an exact portrait of the Ideal X maiden voyage.
Unmarked container hangs level from four corner fittings above an empty period flatbed; cargo vessel is a modest contemporary supporting object.
No printed text, logos, invented charts, injury, caricature or impossible container wheels; calm adult ivory/sage watercolor composition.
